transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-07 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Rajesh Singh (Redwood SE), Oliver Reyes (CSM); Maya Ortiz (Cascade Head of Platform), Tom Beckett (CTO), Rita Sun (SRE Lead), Daniel Cho (Procurement)

Summary:
Quick renewal/check-in focused on committed capacity uplift, adding EU region, and establishing a fallback/playbook for degraded capacity. Discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs and security guardrails for private VPC routing. Agreed on perf run and paperwork next steps.

Topics: committed capacity, eu region onboarding, dedicated vs hosted failover, SOC2/KMS, pricing amendment, perf test plan, rollout/canary strategy, onboarding timeline.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're expecting about 45, 50 minutes today. Quick round robin?
[00:12] Maya (Cascade): Hi, Maya here. I'll hand off to Tom for timeline and procurement.
[00:17] Tom (Cascade): Tom here. We're looking to increase committed capacity by roughly 2x starting April, plus we want EU region enabled for data residency. Procurement also wants clear SLAs and fallback.
[00:30] Rajesh (Redwood SE): Quick clarifying q — when you say 2x, is that peak concurrent or average daily token volume?
[00:37] Rita (Cascade): It's mostly peak concurrent inference sessions for customer-facing assistants, with bursty nights. A lot of the traffic is p95 sensitive.
[00:45] Rajesh (Redwood): Got it. So our recommendations will vary; dedicated pools buy predictable throughput and isolation, hosted is cheaper but you'd rely on routing.
[01:02] Lena: And we discussed last time that you wanted private VPC for some workloads?
[01:05] Maya: Yes, for payment processing prompts we need VPC + KMS. The rest can stay hosted.
[01:12] Daniel (Cascade): From procurement: can we get a single amendment that covers region uplift and an option to burst? We have legal windows in March.
[01:21] Lena: Absolutely, we can draft an amendment. We'll put options for 12- and 18-month terms and show marginal unit economics.
[01:30] Tom: Main questions — how will failover look if EU capacity temporarily drops? We can't have customers see downtime.
[01:40] Rajesh: Two approaches: active-active across regions with geo-routing or active-primary with fallback to a lower-cost model variant in a different region. Both have tradeoffs — cross-region adds latency for EU users if routed to US; fallback to quantized model reduces quality but keeps responses.
[02:05] Rita: Latency is key for us. p95 under 300ms is our bar for core flows. If fallback increases p95 to 600ms, that's hurtful.
[02:16] Rajesh: Right, so there's a playbook: 1) preferred: route to EU dedicated pool; 2) if capacity saturated, automatically route to EU hosted equivalent (if available); 3) if region unavailable, route to the nearest regional model with prefix caching and token-preserving fallbacks; 4) as final fallback serve a short-form cached response or reduce model size. We'll document the thresholds.
[02:45] Lena: We'll include SLO thresholds and automation rules in the amendment so it's operationally clear.
[02:52] Maya: Can you include an example of the failover timeline — like at 85% util what's the action, at 95% what's the canary?
[03:01] Rajesh: Yes. Our canary policy can kick at 90% and we can set automatic burst into a reserve pool for short windows. We'll show sample latency impact table.
[03:12] Tom: Also curious about KV cache warmup across regions — that is a big latency source after failover.
[03:20] Rajesh: Good point. We propose prefix caching replication, but KV is bounded by consistency. So we can pre-warm popular prefixes during a planned failover; for unplanned events there will be some cold-start penalty. We'll quantify that in the perf run.
[03:40] Daniel: On security: SOC2 report, KMS/HSM usage, audit logs — we need to see those artifacts. Also SSO/SAML for access.
[03:50] Oliver: We'll attach SOC2 Type II, KMS integration notes, and the VPC onboarding checklist. SAML/SSO is standard via our console.
[04:03] Maya: Great. Also, does Redwood support customer-managed keys for the private pool?
[04:08] Rajesh: Yes, for Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM. Hosted can use our managed keys or customer keys depending on config, but there are ops differences we will document.
[04:25] Lena: Pricing — we'll show base committed units, uplift pricing for EU region, and burst/overage rates. We'll also include different tiers for quantized model variants.
[04:36] Tom: We want the math side-by-side: current spend vs committed with uplift and the expected monthly savings if we commit.
[04:44] Lena: We'll provide an amortized forecast model.
[04:48] Rita: For the performance run — can we simulate business hours with a 4-hr sustained high load and then a 1-hr burst? We need p95 numbers across scenarios.
[04:58] Rajesh: Yes, we'll run a 4-hour steady-state and 1-hour burst using your prompt set. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 and token cost. Also will test fallback to hosted and to smaller quantized model variant.
[05:15] Tom: How long to provision an EU dedicated pool once contract signed?
[05:20] Rajesh: Typical lead time is 10 to 18 business days depending on capacity and any custom network peering. If we do a staged roll (canary hosts first) we can shorten perceived activation for a subset.
[05:33] Maya: We have compliance checks that expect data residency proof. Can you host logs in-region and show proof for audit?
[05:41] Oliver: Yes, audit logs are region-tagged; we'll show the retention and export options.
[05:47] Daniel: Regarding SLA credits — what's the p99 SLA we can expect for dedicated pools?
[05:53] Lena: Our SLA targets for Dedicated are 99.9% availability and latency SLOs per model profile; we'll include the exact credit matrix in the amendment.
[06:05] Tom: Hypothetical: we sign 18 months with a 2x uplift and an EU dedicated cluster. Do you offer staggered provisioning so we can ramp traffic gradually?
[06:15] Rajesh: Yes, canary rollouts and traffic shaping are part of our rollout playbook. We'll propose a 3-week ramp plan in the runbook.
[06:25] Maya: One more — does Redwood support routing policies by customer tier? We want premium customers routed preferentially during capacity pressure.
[06:32] Rajesh: Yes, weight-based routing and token-priority policies exist; we can show config examples.
[06:40] Speaker 1 (transcript error): um mm, sorry, interjection — are there any limitations around model variants for quantization?
[06:47] Rajesh: Some model architectures see minor quality degradation when aggressively quantized. We'll produce sample eval diffs on your prompt set.
[07:00] Lena: Ok next, procurement questions?
[07:04] Daniel: Taxes and billing — we need consolidated monthly invoice and export of per-route token usage for chargeback. Will that be in the contract?
[07:12] Oliver: Yes we have token-level billing and can supply per-route exports. We'll add billing export cadence to the amendment.
[07:20] Tom: For the perf run, what observability hooks do we get? We'll need traces, latency heatmaps, token breakdown.
[07:29] Rajesh: You'll get per-call token breakdown, per-token latency, and per-model error rates. We'll provide a temporary dashboard for the perf run.
[07:40] Maya: Any specific limitations on VPC NAT throughput or IP whitelisting that we should plan for?
[07:46] Rajesh: We'll share the network sizing doc. Typically egress is the main constraint; we'll confirm required bandwidth in the runbook.
[07:58] Lena: Recap: we will prepare a pricing amendment with EU uplift and burst rates, Rajesh runs perf test, Oliver shares SOC2/KMS/VPC docs, Cascade to share prompt set and traffic profiles. Decision window targeted mid-February.
[08:15] Tom: Sounds good. We'll aim to confirm term length (12 v 18) by Feb 18.
[08:21] Maya: Also please include example rollback steps in case a region becomes unhealthy.
[08:26] Rajesh: We'll add a rollback checklist and a sample playbook for manual and automated rollback.
[08:33] Rita: One last thing — can we reserve some buffer for short-term burst capacity during Black Friday-like events?
[08:40] Lena: Yes, burst credits can be pre-bought or enabled as a reserved buffer in the amendment. We'll show both options.
[08:50] Daniel: Procurement will need a statement of work level detail for the onboarding tasks.
[08:55] Oliver: We'll include an SOW appendix in the amendment.
[09:00] Tom: Great. Anything else?
[09:03] Lena: Nope, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the items on the thread.

Notes on transcript quality: some speaker labels are approximate; a few words mis-transcribed (e.g., KV cache typed as KV cat in places). There was a short cross-talk at ~06:40.
